## 30,000 euros for the surroundings: beyond the limits of the wetland

The exterior intervention responds to a logic that goes beyond mere ornamentation. The Motril City Council has allocated a budget of nearly 30,000 euros to condition the perimeter of the Charca de Suárez, a space that until now functioned as a diffuse border between the urban fabric and the protected ecosystem. The work includes the creation of a specific parking area, the installation of urban furniture, and the improvement of pedestrian access connecting the wetland with the urban center. This is an intervention that, without touching a single hectare of floodable land, aims to modify the daily relationship of the people of Motril with this enclave.

The planned parking area resolves a shortcoming that regular visitors knew well. Until now, vehicles accumulated on the margins of the access road, creating risk situations for pedestrians and an image not in keeping with the educational vocation of the space. The new parking area will be located at a strategic point that can absorb weekend influx without visually invading the landscape. Municipal technicians have insisted that the intervention will be carried out with permeable materials and chromatic integration that minimizes the impact on the immediate surroundings.

The planned urban furniture includes benches, trash bins, and information panels distributed along the access route. The choice of these elements is not coincidental: each bench will be oriented toward specific points of the wetland where birdwatching is most fruitful, while the panels will offer updated information about the species present in each season. The trash bins, for their part, respond to a recurring demand from visitors themselves, who sometimes found themselves forced to carry their waste throughout the entire route. The installation of these elements seeks to normalize the visit without turning the environment into a conventional urban park.

The improvement of pedestrian access constitutes the backbone of the entire intervention. The current layout presents uneven terrain and unpaved sections that hinder transit for people with reduced mobility, a group that until now found serious barriers to approaching the wetland. The work will include regularization of the surface, elimination of unnecessary steps, and the creation of a continuous route from the last streets of the neighborhood to the entrance of the enclosure. This intervention connects directly with the philosophy of the new Interpretation Center, which already incorporated ramps and accessible spaces in its original design.

The integration of the wetland into the social fabric of Motril is the ultimate goal of this budget allocation. The Charca de Suárez has ceased to be a space reserved for naturalists and ornithologists to become a place for strolling, meeting, and learning for the entire citizenry. Municipal officials understand that effective conservation of a natural space involves generating emotional bonds with the population that surrounds it, and those bonds are also built at the access points, on the benches where a family rests after a walk, or on the panel that explains to a child which bird has just crossed the sky.

The pedestrian connection with the urban center deserves specific mention. The route to be conditioned starts from the vicinity of the San Antonio neighborhood and runs through land that for years functioned as a no-man's-land between the city and the wetland. The intervention will transform that route into a pleasant walk, illuminated where necessary and signposted with clear criteria. The distance between the center of Motril and the entrance to the Charca remains the same, but the perception of the journey will change completely: it will no longer be an uncomfortable trip to a remote place, but a pleasant itinerary that anticipates the wetland experience.

The 30,000-euro allocation is part of a broader universal accessibility strategy that the city council has been applying to its public facilities. The Charca de Suárez could not remain outside that policy, especially after the million-euro investment destined for its interior. It would be contradictory to have a model interpretation center and accessible walkways if a visitor with reduced mobility could not reach the door. The coherence between the inside and outside of the wetland is precisely what this intervention aims to guarantee.

The execution deadlines are relatively short, given that these are works of low technical complexity. The municipal forecast points to the work being completed before the start of the next high visitor season, which coincides with the spring months and the migratory passage of numerous species. That schedule will allow the immediate verification of the effect of the improvements on public attendance and on the distribution of visitors in the surroundings. Attendance data from recent years, which exceed tens of thousands of people annually, support the need for this intervention.

The exterior intervention does not modify a single square meter of the protected wetland area. All work is carried out on municipally owned land located outside the perimeter of the wetland, which avoids any impact on the flora and fauna that constitute the heart of this space. The separation between the scope of the work and the ecosystem is strict, with perimeter fencing that will be maintained throughout the execution. This caution responds to the growing sensitivity of the local administration toward an enclave that aspires to soon obtain designation as a Special Protection Area for Birds.

The investment in the exterior surroundings completes a circle that began with the recovery of the lagoons, continued with the construction of the interpretation center, and is now reinforced with the dignification of the access points. Each of these pieces responds to the same idea: the Charca de Suárez is not a space isolated from urban life, but a natural extension of Motril that deserves to be treated with the same care as any other public facility. The 30,000 euros allocated to this phase is a modest amount compared to the overall project budget, but its impact on the daily experience of visitors can be disproportionately high.

The choice of materials and the design of the furniture elements has been carried out with criteria of durability and low maintenance. The benches will be made of reinforced concrete with a technical wood finish, resistant to environmental salinity and the intense solar exposure that characterizes this stretch of the Granada coast. The information panels will use galvanized metal supports and printed sheets with ultraviolet protection, so that the information remains legible for years without needing frequent replacements. The experience accumulated in other natural spaces in the municipality has served to avoid design errors that in the long run make maintenance more expensive.

Universal accessibility is not limited to the elimination of physical barriers. The information panels will incorporate QR codes that link to content adapted for people with visual or hearing disabilities, a measure that expands the reach of information without needing to duplicate physical supports. This technological solution, of reduced cost, allows the visit experience to be more complete for all audiences. The Charca de Suárez thus positions itself as a reference in accessibility within the network of natural spaces managed by local administrations in Andalusia.

The exterior surroundings of the Charca have for years been the great forgotten element of successive municipal interventions. While the interior of the wetland received million-euro investments and was consolidated as a sanctuary for birdlife, the access points remained in a state of provisionality that contrasted with the quality of the natural resource. The now-announced allocation corrects that imbalance and sends a clear message: the visitor experience begins long before crossing the gate of the enclosure. An orderly parking area, an accessible walkway, and dignified furniture are the prelude that a space of this relevance deserves.

The connection between this intervention and the future ZEPA designation is evident. The influx of visitors expected after obtaining that European protection status requires an environment capable of absorbing the pressure without degrading. The 30,000 euros invested now are a preventive measure that will avoid greater problems in the future, when the Charca de Suárez appears in nature guides across the continent. The local administration has understood that conservation and public use are not opposing objectives, but complementary dimensions of the same policy.

Residents of the neighboring neighborhoods will be the first beneficiaries of this improvement. For them, the Charca de Suárez is not a tourist destination but a space of proximity, a place to walk at sunset or take the children to see the first black-winged stilts of the season. The dignification of pedestrian access reinforces that daily use and consolidates the wetland as another neighborhood facility, with the particularity that its programming is dictated by nature and not by the municipal agenda. That neighborhood dimension is, perhaps, the best guarantee of long-term protection for this unique enclave on the Granada coast.
